title: Latency burst probe — personal runbook
content:
Context:
Quick informal tracker for a set of small runs investigating short-lived latency bursts under different batching and KV cache warmup patterns. Goal is to capture noisy runs, jot hypotheses, and keep commands + alt-configs handy.

High-level notes (scratch):
- Problem: ~200ms p95 spikes observed when concurrent short requests hit cold KV cache combined with small batch windows.
- Hypothesis A: prefix KV cache misses + inefficient kernel selection for short seq_len cause transient p95 spikes.
- Hypothesis B: autoscaler / preemption on Dedicated nodes creates a short-term scheduling jitter (rare).
- Quick experiment goal: reproduce reliably with synthetic client, then test two mitigations: (1) pre-warm prefix cache, (2) force smaller slab allocation / disable continuous batching.

Run table (personal shorthand):
ID | date | model | hw | batch | seq | quant | kv_warm | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | thrpt(tok/s) | cost_est | notes
R-101 | 2025-11-03 | redwood-v1-13b-q4 | A100-80GB | 1 | 64 | q4_0 | no | 38 | 210 | 420 | $0.0009 | single-request synthetic, baseline spike observed
R-102 | 2025-11-03 | redwood-v1-13b-q4 | A100-80GB | 4 | 64 | q4_0 | no | 45 | 290 | 1200 | $0.0012 | batching increased p95 (coalescing delay?)
R-103 | 2025-11-04 | redwood-v1-13b-q4 | A100-80GB | 1 | 64 | q4_0 | yes(pre) | 36 | 58 | 410 | $0.0009 | pre-warm drastically reduced p95, strong signal for KV importance
R-118 | 2025-11-07 | mistral-7B-int8 | H100 | 1 | 32 | int8 | no | 22 | 85 | 760 | $0.0006 | lower cost, spikes still present but smaller magnitude
R-134 | 2025-12-01 | redwood-v1-13b-q4 | A100-80GB | 1 | 64 | q4_0 | no | 40 | 220 | 400 | $0.0009 | ran under Dedicated reserved pool, observed small scheduling jitter at 02:10 UTC
R-140 | 2025-12-02 | redwood-v1-13b-q4 | A100-80GB | 1 | 64 | q4_0 | yes(runtime) | 37 | 60 | 410 | $0.0009 | runtime-level KV caching + sticky routing enabled, stable

Commands / quick repro notes:
- Synthetic client (looping single short request, 50 qps burst):
  python tools/synthetic_client.py --model redwood-v1-13b-q4 --concurrency 12 --qps 50 --seq 64 --duration 120 --warmup 10
- Forced config toggle (local debug env):
  RUNTIME_FLAGS="DISABLE_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=1 DEBUG_KV_PREFETCH=1" ./bin/serve --model redwood-v1-13b-q4 --device a100
- Small perf snippet collected via perf-trace (local):
  [2025-11-03 14:12] trace: kernel_select(ms): 1.2 | kv_fetch(ms): 17.8 | batch_coalesce(ms): 3.6

Open questions / followups:
- Re-run on H100 private pool with identical config to verify hardware effect (booked for 2026-02-01 but blocked by infra quota).
- Is there an internal flag to prioritize prefix cache loads for short requests? File a small RFC if not.
- Can service layer expose a per-route prewarm option at SDK level? Good for mobile short requests.

Quick action items (personal):
- [ ] Add a small unit-test to synthetic_client to assert p95 < 100ms with kv_warm=true for seq<=64. (PR draft: github #412)
- [ ] Ask SRE if autoscaler logs show preemption events near timestamps from R-134. (INF-872)
- [ ] Prototype a small prewarm job that triggers per-route stub before peak (script in /tools/prewarm-route.sh)

Random scratch (notes-to-self):
- When copying numbers into confluence, include exact flags used (kv_warm method: batch prefetch vs runtime sticky).
- If I can't reproduce reliably, instrument the client with timestamps + request ids and dump to s3 for later join.

Yesterday's quick sketch of prometheus query I used:
- p95 latency per route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/api/ai/.*"}[5m])) by (le))

References / links used:
- infra ticket (check): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-872
- PR that toggled batch_coalesce: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412

End of sheet — will keep appending runs here and mark final summary when I have a reproducible mitigation.
